title: Ephemeral debug orchestrator and safe probe runner for on-call diagnostics
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: On-call responders often need short-lived, read-only probes (log tailing, metric snapshot, safe config queries) that run in an isolated environment and do not change runtime state. The incident-bot currently supports scripted runbooks but lacks an opinionated, safe orchestration layer for ephemeral diagnostics. This PR introduces an Ephemeral Debug Orchestrator and a Safe Probe Runner that: (1) schedules and executes pre-approved diagnostic probes in a sandbox, (2) enforces time/CPU/memory limits and read-only constraints, (3) automatically collects artifacts and attaches them to the incident context, and (4) provides a responder-facing CLI and HTTP endpoints gated by a feature flag. Changes are opt-in and behind INCIDENT_EPHEMERAL_DEBUG with granular RBAC checks.

What this PR contains: - new orchestrator that manages probe lifecycle, lease tokens, and backoff for noisy systems - a safeexec sandbox with syscall restrictions, chroot-like file access limiting, and per-probe resource caps - probe registry with small curated probes (logs-sample, metric-snapshot, config-dump-readonly) - responder CLI helpers (tools/oncall/ephemeral-cli) for requesting a probe and downloading artifacts - observability: probe metrics, traces, and audit events for every probe run - e2e tests that run probes against a local fake target and validate sandbox constraints

Design notes: The orchestrator uses the existing worker queue but adds a short-lived lease manager (15s - 5m) to ensure probes do not hang. Probes are run inside safeexec and are strictly read-only wrappers around existing diagnostic utilities. Results are uploaded to the incident attachment store with tags indicating sensitivity level. The orchestrator defaults to deny for non-admins; requester must have the new permission scope "incident:ephemeral_probe:invoke".

Migration & rollout plan: - Feature gated by INCIDENT_EPHEMERAL_DEBUG=false by default. - Step 1: Deploy with flag disabled and telemetry only (probe_attempts metric) - Step 2: Enable for a small pilot SRE squad and manual canary (1 week) - Step 3: Gradual enable for all on-call rotations with opt-out controls.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation of orchestrator and sandbox - [x] Unit tests for safeexec restrictions - [x] Integration tests for lease/timeouts - [x] Documentation (tools/oncall/ephemeral-cli.md) - [x] Feature flag + RBAC entries - [x] Observability dashboards (minimal)

Security considerations: The sandbox uses seccomp-style filtering and disallows network egress. All probe binaries are run with a dedicated, unprivileged UID. The code path records full audit events and stores artifacts in an access-controlled bucket. We intentionally avoided any writable access to production config or mutation APIs.

Operational notes: The orchestrator emits probe_attempts, probe_success, probe_failure, probe_timeout, and probe_resource_violation metrics. Alerts are suggested in the README for probe_failure rate spikes. The PR also adds a backpressure policy to avoid overwhelming a target service during repeated probe runs.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz (2024-11-13): Important PR — please call out failure modes and ensure we do not allow probes to hit high-cardinality logs. Also request explicit test demonstrating resource limit enforcement.
Aisha Patel (2024-11-14): Reply: added resource enforcement unit tests and a 'probe_resource_violation' metric. We also added throttling on probe attempts per-incident to limit cardinality.
Linnea Sørensen (2024-11-15): Suggestion: extract seccomp profile to a reusable package and add CI lint for profiles. Also request a short diagram in docs showing artifact flow.

Aisha Patel (2024-11-16): Reply: extracted profile to internal/safeexec/profiles.go and added profile lint step to CI. Documentation updated with artifact flow diagram in tools/oncall/ephemeral-cli.md.

Devon Carter (2024-11-18): nits on log messages and retry backoff parameters. Also noted an e2e flake on CI (timing) — recommended increasing backoff and explicit sleep in the fake target to stabilize test.

Aisha Patel (2024-11-19): Reply: increased backoff, improved logging to include probe_id and lease token, and addressed the e2e flake with a deterministic readiness handshake in the test harness. CI green on final run.
ci_summary: Initial CI run: lint failed (seccomp profile naming). Second run: lint fixed; e2e flaky due to timing; third run: added deterministic readiness and retry backoff; final run passed. Total checks: 8 passed, 0 failed.
release_notes: Add ephemeral diagnostic orchestration and a safe probe runner for on-call. Feature gated behind INCIDENT_EPHEMERAL_DEBUG and protected by new RBAC scope incident:ephemeral_probe:invoke. Includes CLI, observability, and e2e tests.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover sandbox syscall filtering and resource limits. Integration tests validate lease expiration and artifact uploads. e2e uses a fake target to validate read-only constraints. Recommend enabling feature flag in staging and monitoring probe_failure and probe_resource_violation metrics during canary.
motivation_summary: Provide responders with a safe, auditable way to run short-lived diagnostics during incidents without risking production mutations or noisy repeated probes.
